verdict.rationale: Omarchy is a Linux distribution that runs entirely on the user's own hardware. The docs show an ISO you write to USB and install, plus dual-boot, unattended installs and a VM option, and community users report installing it themselves on their own machines. A public GitHub repo (basecamp/omarchy) also exists. missing for 10: explicit documentation of open-source licensing or building from source, and independence from upstream Arch package mirrors for fully self-contained operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Write the ISO to a USB stick and answer five questions. It hands back a finished desktop.
The manual also covers [dual booting beside Windows](/manual/dual-boot-install/) and [unattended installs](/manual/unattended-installs/).
All of Omarchy running in a virtual machine, so you can get a taste first.
Omarchy 2.0 ships as an Arch-based ISO, and installation is fairly quick (~5 minutes on a fresh machine) given decent bandwidth.
